descript.abstract: A mapped waste site may contain more than one polygon, line, and/or point feature. This shapefile contains a representation of all of the point, line and polygon features that make up mapped waste sites at the Department of Energy's Hanford Site. The spatial data in this shapefile was compiled from many different sources including translation from annotated field maps, estimates based on published reports, digitizing from aerial photography and scanned drawings, and global positioning surveys. The mapped location is based on the best available information. As more information is acquired through the declassification of documents and photos, newly identiifed drawings, and field work associated with remediation planning, the mapped location is modified to account for the newly identified information. None of the WIDS mapping is absolute. Waste sites, especially associated pipelines, may have been modified in the field without ever updating the design drawing. In some cases, excavation has shown that the construction and location of a waste site was completely different from what is shown on approved "as-built" drawings.
descript.purpose: The purpose of this shape file is to indicate the location of known or suspected waste sites. The mapped location provide a starting basis for remediation planning and field activities. The mapped sites are also used during excavation and drilling activities to identifying potential hazards at the work site.

secinfo.sechandl: Some information mapped in this dataset has been determined to be sensitive with regard to the location of facilities that might be terrorist targets. Information can only be passed to non-Hanford entities on an "as needed" basis. Before any such data transfer, a classification officer should be contacted.

citeinfo.othercit: The ehsit.shp file was created by merging object data from the ehsitirp, ehsitpip and ehsitpir shape files. The line data in ehsitpip were buffered to a distance of .5 meters. The point data in ehsitpir were buffered to a distance of .5 meters. The two buffered sets were merged with the polygon data in ehsitirp. The boundaries between the resulting data were dissolved on the Site_Num field. This allows a search for a WIDS site as a single object instead of a group of points, lines and polygons.

procstep.procdesc: The ehsit.shp file was created by merging object data from the ehsitirp, ehsitpip and ehsitpir shape files. The line data in ehsitpip were buffered to a distance of .5 meters. The point data in ehsitpir were buffered to a distance of .5 meters. The two buffered sets were merged with the polygon data in ehsitirp. The boundaries between the resulting data were dissolved on the Site_Num field. This allows a search for a WIDS site as a single object instead of a group of points, lines and polygons.
The shapefile attributes are updated with WIDS data from the WIDS database. This is done by SQL Data Transformation Services.

New fields ERS_CL_RCL and ERS_OP_DES are added for symbolization purposes. ERS_CL_RCL is the concatenation of the ERS_CLASS and ERS_RECLAS fields. ERS_OP_DES is the description of the operable units in 200 areas. This field is taken from the field ERS_OPRUNT. This is done by Data Transformation Services.
The WIDS shapefile is imported into SDE geodatabase.

Matches to the WIDS "Site" table, "SiteCode" field. This field is a unique code assigned to a site that is created during site identification and is automatically generated by the database system. For new sites, the Site Code is automatically assigned by the database when the potential site is entered into the database. It is given a prefix indicating the designated area in which the site is located (such as 100-D, 200-E, 300, 600, etc.), followed by the next sequential number from the previously entered site for that area. For sites entered in the database prior to reengineering of the WIDS (1995), the site code was generally assigned in accordance with the facility-naming convention at the time it was entered. Some site codes were modified during database reengineering, such as converting very long names to initials, to be more consistent with current practices. Older names were added to the Site Names field.
Matches to the WIDS "Site" table, "SiteID" field. This field is a unique number automatically assigned to a site when first entered into the database using the next sequential number.
Matches to the WIDS "RegulatoryInfo" table, "ResponsibleContractor" field. This field is the name of the contractor or subcontractor responsible for the site.

Matches to the WIDS "RegulatoryInfo" table, "DOEDivision" field. This field is the Department of Energy (DOE) Division within the Richland Operations Office (RL) or the Office of River Protection (ORP) that is responsible for the waste site.
Matches to the WIDS "Site" table, "DesgArea" field. This field indicates where the site is located at the Hanford Site.

Matches to the WIDS "Site" table, "SiteClassificationStatus" field. This field is the classification of the site in terms of its status in the database. The purpose is to distinguish sites by their database status. The WIDS contains accepted, rejected, and discovery sites. Rejected sites are flagged as "Rejected (Proposed)" until they receive concurrence from the lead regulatory agency.

Matches to the WIDS "Site" table, "OperUnit" field. This field is the operable unit in which the site has been assigned. An operable unit at the Hanford Site is a group of land disposal sites placed together for the purposes of doing a Remedial Investigation/Feasibility Study (RI/FS) and subsequent cleanup actions. The primary criteria for placement of a site into an operable unit includes geographic proximity, similarity of waste characteristics and site type, and the possibility for economies of scale.
Matches to the WIDS "Site" table, "SiteReclassStatus" field. This field is the status of a site after being changed from an "accepted" classification per TPA-MP-14 (Ecology et al. 1998).
Matches to the WIDS "Site" table, "SiteStatus" field. This field indicates the current operational status of the unit.

Matches to the WIDS "Site" table, "SiteType" field. This field is the type of structure for the site. Generally, types are defined by the waste within them or in the case of structures, the processing function performed.
Matches to the WIDS "Site" table, "SiteNames" field. This field is the common or working names by which the site is known, including any/all aliases for a site.

Matches to the WIDS "RegulatoryInfo" table, "SWMUFlag" field. This field indicates if the site is a solid waste management unit (SWMU) as specified under Washington Administrative Code (WAC) WAC 173-303-040.
Matches to the WIDS "RegulatoryInfo" table, "UnitCategory" field. This field is the code for the regulatory program with authority over the waste site.
